=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 19-102 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide and restore failures return success, so callers cannot detect that credentials were not safely hidden or restored.
  WHY: The helper exits 0 on failure paths, allowing workflows to proceed as if credential isolation succeeded.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 77-83 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore verifies only that origin uses github.com, not that it is the trusted repository, before injecting GH_TOKEN.
  WHY: An editor-changed origin for another GitHub repository passes the host-only check and receives the workflow token.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 76-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore does not validate remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf rewrites before injecting credentials.
  WHY: A push destination can be redirected to an attacker-controlled repository while the fetch origin passes validation.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 85-93 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore reinstates captured extraheaders at their original scope instead of scoping authorization to the verified repository origin.
  WHY: A host-wide extraheader can send the token on GitHub requests to repositories other than the verified origin. Severity disagreement: some reviewers rated this major; the highest reported severity is blocker.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 19-54 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Hide does not validate GITHUB_REPOSITORY before stripping credentials.
  WHY: Without a trusted repository identity, hide still removes credentials and exits successfully. Severity disagreement: some reviewers rated this major; the highest reported severity is blocker.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 62-97 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: Restore mutates each checkout as it processes it instead of validating all checkouts before injecting credentials into any of them.
  WHY: If a later checkout fails validation, earlier checkouts may already contain GH_TOKEN. Severity disagreement: some reviewers rated this major; the highest reported severity is blocker.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:666-675 | severity=high | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna, qwen_qwen3_7-plus]
  PROBLEM: _diagnostic_fingerprint hashes the literal "unavailable" sentinel instead of preserving it as missing data.
  WHY: Prompt rendering can present a hash as though a missing diagnostic were a real fingerprint. Severity disagreement: reviewers rated this from nit to major; the highest reported severity is major.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:660-663 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  PROBLEM: _diagnostic_text and its _DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS dependency are unreferenced dead code after text sanitization was replaced by fingerprinting.
  WHY: The unused code can mislead readers about which sanitization path is active.
- README.md:1402-1416 | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The README documents credential-restoration guarantees that the implementation does not enforce.
  WHY: It claims repository identity, push destination, and extraheader scope are verified when the helper does not provide those guarantees.
- agents.md:209-226 | severity=medium | confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The agents documentation makes credential-restoration and diagnostic-prompt claims that the implementation does not enforce.
  WHY: The documented security and prompt behavior diverges from runtime behavior.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:24-55 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The editor can delete or truncate the marker used by restore, leaving credentials stripped with no restoration path.
  WHY: The marker is in an editor-writable directory and restore relies on its contents.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:27-28 | severity=medium | confidence=[4]
  flagged_by: [minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: If marker creation fails, hide continues removing credentials without recording a restore path.
  WHY: A later restore cannot recover credentials that were removed without a marker.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
- requirement: "The credential helper rejects failed hides/restores and restores auth only when the origin still names the workflow's original repository (or its trusted support checkout) and its push URL agrees, not an editor-changed GitHub destination; generic GitHub extraheaders are restored scoped to the verified origin only."
  expected_change_site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh hide and restore paths; .github/workflows/implement.yml implement-editor launches; scripts/run_plan_codex.sh plan-editor launches
  confidence=[5]
  flagged_by: [deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro, google_gemini-3_8-flash, minimax_minimax-m3, qwen_qwen3_7-plus, z-ai_glm-5_2]
  EVIDENCE: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh lacks GITHUB_REPOSITORY validation, pushurl/pushInsteadOf checks, repo-scoped extraheader restoration, pre-validation of all checkouts, and non-zero failure exits; tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py asserts these behaviors but the implementation is absent; .github/workflows/implement.yml and scripts/run_plan_codex.sh have the credential-hide/restore launches, while the env-scrub half is reported as wired correctly.
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM deepseek_deepseek-v4-pro ===
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 19-54 (hide) and 56-101 (restore), culminating at line 102 `exit 0` | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Every failure path in hide and restore exits successfully.
  WHY: Callers cannot detect failed credential isolation; the tests at tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:45-46, line 100, and lines 137-138 expect non-zero exits.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 77-83 (origin restore case in the case block) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Restore checks only that origin starts with `https://github.com/`, not that it names the expected repository.
  WHY: An editor-changed attacker repository passes validation and receives GH_TOKEN.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 77-93 (entire restore case block) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Restore does not inspect remote.origin.pushurl or url.*.pushInsteadOf configuration.
  WHY: Pushes can be redirected to an attacker repository despite an unchanged fetch origin.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Lines 62-97 (restore loop over marker entries) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Restore injects credentials into each checkout before validating later checkouts.
  WHY: A later validation failure leaves credentials in earlier checkouts.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:Lines 130-139 (test_hide_fails_without_trusted_repository_identity) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The test expects hide to fail without GITHUB_REPOSITORY, but the script neither reads that variable nor fails.
  WHY: The test's non-zero return-code and credential-remains assertions fail.
- tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py:Lines 67-77, 80-90, and 142-157 | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: Three tests assert push-destination checks and atomic pre-validation that the script does not perform.
  WHY: Restore succeeds and injects the token, so the tests' failure and configuration assertions fail.
- scripts/workflow_failure_heal_evidence.py:Lines 660-663 and line 108 | severity=low | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: `_diagnostic_text` and `_DIAGNOSTIC_CHARS` have no callers outside their own definitions and use.
  WHY: The dead code may mislead readers about whether step names are still text-filtered.
- scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh:Line 1-102 (entire script) | severity=critical | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The credential helper does not enforce the documented trust boundary for editor launches.
  WHY: It does not verify repository identity or push destinations and does not report failures through its exit code.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The credential helper rejects failed hides/restores and restores auth only when the origin still names the workflow's original repository (or its trusted support checkout) and its push URL agrees, not an editor-changed GitHub destination; generic GitHub extraheaders are restored scoped to the verified origin only." (README.md lines 1407-1412, agents.md lines 218-224)
  Expected change site: scripts/editor_git_credentials.sh — the restore case block (lines 56-101) and the hide path (lines 19-54)
  Evidence of absence: No GITHUB_REPOSITORY check exists anywhere in the script. No pushurl or pushInsteadOf inspection exists. Extraheaders are restored at their captured scope rather than scoped to the verified repository origin. The restore loop processes checkouts sequentially rather than atomically. All failure paths exit 0. The tests at lines 67-77, 80-90, 130-139, and 142-157 of tests/test_heal_evidence_editor_isolation.py encode the expected behavior, but none of those validations exist in the script.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
